title: Laws of character
hook: diet, sleep, speech and health are spiritual practice

segments.voice: Yesterday, ahavah and yirah, and your line: love and awe. What living thing did you stop and really look at? Day one thousand one hundred forty-five.

Early in a book about knowing God, the subject changes. Suddenly there's advice about when to eat. Not to eat unless you're hungry. Not to drink unless you're thirsty. Not to fill your stomach all the way, but to stop while there's still some room. Advice about sleep. Advice about how much to talk. It sits in the Book of Knowledge, not far from the foundation of foundations, and it's written in the same voice as the laws about God.
screen: `A BOOK ABOUT KNOWING GOD.` → `THEN: WHEN TO EAT.` → `SAME BOOK, SAME VOICE.`

segments.voice: De'ot. Usually translated character, or dispositions: the settled habits of a person's temper. Hilkhot De'ot, the laws of character. Earlier this block we heard Maimonides on the middle way. Today is about where he takes it next: into the body. Turn it four ways. First, the reason. Maimonides says that keeping the body healthy and whole is part of the ways of God, because a sick person can't understand or know the Creator. A body in pain pulls the mind away. So caring for it isn't vanity. It's clearing the road. Second, the details. He gets specific. Eat when hungry. Stop before you're full; he says to stop at about a quarter short of full. Don't eat in a rush. Sleep enough, and at night. He even writes about exercise before meals. This is a law code, and it reads in places like a doctor's note. Third, the intention. Here's the turn that makes it spiritual. Maimonides says a person should eat, drink, sleep and work with one aim: a healthy body, so that the soul can serve God. Then he goes further. Someone who lives that way serves God all the time, even while sleeping, because the rest is taken in order to serve. Sleep becomes a kind of worship, not because of what happens during it, but because of why. Fourth, speech. He brings it into the same chapters. Speak about wisdom and kindness. Say less. The old teaching from Pirkei Avot, that silence is a fence for wisdom, sits behind his advice. Diet, sleep, speech, health. Ordinary days, with a reason running underneath.
screen: `DE'OT: SETTLED HABITS OF CHARACTER.` · `A HEALTHY BODY CLEARS THE ROAD.` · `EAT, SLEEP, WORK FOR ONE AIM.` · `SAY LESS.` · then, large: `THE BODY SERVES THE SOUL.`

segments.voice: Today's practice is to eat one meal mindfully. Right now, let this sit be a rehearsal. Settle, and breathe. Notice whether you're hungry, honestly, or just used to eating at this hour. Then picture your next meal. See yourself sitting down, not rushing. Tasting the first bite. Pausing halfway to ask how full you are. Stopping with a little room left. If you say a blessing before eating, imagine saying it slowly. Then come back to the breath. The bell holds the time.
De'ot. Character, the settled habits of a person; and Hilkhot De'ot, Maimonides' laws of character, where eating, sleeping and speaking are done for the soul's sake. Today's word.
Your line: the body serves the soul. Today, at one meal, stop with a little room left, and notice what that feels like an hour later. Day one thousand one hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: Some Jews study Hilkhot De'ot as practical guidance for daily habits, and Jews who keep the tradition say blessings before and after eating, turning ordinary meals into moments of attention.
